**VERDICT: REJECT** **Overall Assessment**: The component is functionally incomplete for assistive technology users. It renders a dynamic notification as a plain `
` with zero ARIA roles, no live region declaration, and an auto-dismiss timing that conflicts with screen reader reading speeds. Keyboard users have no dismissal mechanism. This fails the WAI-ARIA APG Toast pattern and multiple WCAG 2.2 criteria. The design requires structural and interaction model fixes before implementation. **Pre-commitment Predictions**: Based on component type (Toast/Notification), I predicted: 1. Missing `role="alert"` or `aria-live` region (AT will not announce the message) 2. Auto-dismiss timing < 3s incompatible with AT reading speed 3. No keyboard dismiss mechanism 4. Visual toast type indicator not communicated programmatically 5. Potential focus management gap on mount Actual findings confirmed all predictions. The component is a visual-only notification with no assistive technology communication layer. **Critical Findings** (blocks access): 1. **Missing live region declaration and ARIA role for dynamic content.** See `BuggyToast.tsx:23-25` where the toast renders as a plain `
` without `role="alert"` or `aria-live`. Screen readers will not announce the message upon mount, nor when it updates. Per WCAG 4.1.3 (Status Messages) and WAI-ARIA APG Toast pattern, dynamic notifications must use `role="alert"` with `aria-live="assertive"` for urgent messages, or `role="status"` with `aria-live="polite"` for non-urgent. Fix: Add `role="alert" aria-live="assertive" aria-atomic="true"` to the container. If multiple toasts can stack, use a single hidden live region that receives messages via state management instead of inline roles. 2. **Auto-dismiss timing conflicts with assistive technology reading speed.** See `BuggyToast.tsx:4` (`duration = 3000`) and `BuggyToast.tsx:10` (`setIsVisible(false)`). Screen readers typically read at 150–200 words per minute. A 3-second timeout will likely truncate the announcement before completion, causing information loss. Per WCAG 4.1.3 and WAI-ARIA APG Toast pattern, toast timers must be adjustable or pauseable, and default durations should accommodate AT reading speed (typically ≥5s for short messages, with user controls to pause/resume).
